title: Minimal EFC Effective Field Theory Ansatz: Scalar-Tensor and Vector-Tensor Formulations with Gravitational Slip from Entropy Gradients
description: Proposes a minimal effective field theory completion for Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) in two formulations: a Horndeski-like scalar–tensor EFT and a vector–tensor EFT with a dynamical energy-flow 4-vector. Both are driven by a sigmoid entropy field S(a) that ensures GR recovery at high redshift and targets a mid‑z signature with weakened growth (mu < 1), gravitational slip (eta > 1), and enhanced lensing (Sigma > 1). The note defines the observables, derives the slip mechanism from entropy-gradient anisotropic stress, and specifies stability/consistency conditions, with numerical evaluation deferred to hi_class/EFTCosmoMC.
keywords: effective field theory of dark energy
author: Morten Magnusson

metric_perturbations.description: Conformal Newtonian (longitudinal) gauge for scalar perturbations; in GR without anisotropic stress one has \Phi = \Psi.

gravitational_slip.description: Definition of gravitational slip; GR corresponds to \eta = 1. Here \eta > 1 implies |\Phi| > |\Psi| and enhances the lensing potential.

mu_definition.description: Effective Newton's constant entering the matter growth equation; GR gives \mu = 1.

sigma_definition.description: Effective lensing strength combining \mu and slip \eta; reduces to \Sigma=1 in GR.

slip_constraint_eq8.description: Constraint linking \eta, \mu, and \Sigma; with \mu<1 and \Sigma>1, this requires \eta>1 in the transition regime.

entropy_sigmoid.description: EFC sigmoid entropy field governing the GR-to-modified-gravity transition; S→0 at early times, S→1 today, with peak derivative at a=a_t.

growth_mu_ansatz.description: Phenomenological growth-response used in the pipeline; yields \mu<1 in the transition while recovering GR at high z.

key_results.main_finding: A minimal EFC EFT driven by a sigmoid entropy field can, in principle, realize the target mid‑z signature (mu < 1, eta > 1, Sigma > 1) either via Horndeski-like braiding/Planck-mass running or via entropy-gradient anisotropic stress in a vector–tensor completion, subject to stability and CMB-compatibility constraints and pending numerical validation.

sealed_predictions.statement: In the transition regime 0.5 < z < 1.5, the observables satisfy mu(z) ≈ 0.925 ± 0.02, Sigma(z) ≳ 1.05, and consequently eta(z) ≈ 1.27 via eta > 2 Sigma / mu − 1, with GR recovery (mu, Sigma, eta → 1) at high redshift.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint RSD (DESI) + cosmic shear and galaxy–galaxy lensing (KiDS/DES/LSST) + CMB lensing (Planck/ACT/S4) tomographic reconstruction of {mu(z), Sigma(z)} in 0.5 < z < 1.5.

sealed_predictions.statement: The time profile of modifications follows the sigmoid S(a) with a transition at a_t ≈ 0.30 (z_t ≈ 2.3) and width Delta ≈ 0.3, implying dS/d ln a peaks near z ≈ 2.3 and drives nonzero braiding (alpha_B) and slip.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Reconstruction of time-dependent EFT alphas from multi-probe data (hi_class/EFTCosmoMC fits) showing peak deviations inconsistent with a sigmoid centered at a_t ≈ 0.30.

sealed_predictions.statement: Vector–tensor realization: a nonzero entropy–flow coupling beta induces a positive gravitational slip (eta − 1 > 0) correlated with the background entropy gradient amplitude, while respecting alpha_T = 0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Constraints on anisotropic stress from lensing–clustering consistency tests that bound (eta − 1) < 0.02 across 0.5 < z < 1.5, independent of screening and consistent with GR.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-precision multi-probe analyses find Sigma(z) ≤ 1.00 ± 0.01 across 0.5 < z < 1.5 while mu(z) < 1, implying eta ≤ 1 and violating the EFC target inequality eta > 2 Sigma / mu − 1.
KC2: Joint RSD + weak-lensing + CMB-lensing reconstructions constrain gravitational slip to eta(z) = 1.00 ± 0.05 for 0.5 < z < 1.5, leaving no room for the required slip from entropy gradients.

KC3: Stable (no-ghost, c_s^2 > 0), luminal (alpha_T = 0) regions of parameter space in the scalar–tensor EFT cannot produce mu < 1, eta > 1, and Sigma > 1 simultaneously in hi_class/EFTCosmoMC, for any {B0, M0, a_t, Delta} consistent with early-time GR recovery (S → 0).

KC4: Vector–tensor implementation yields negligible anisotropic stress with robust upper bounds implying (eta − 1) < 0.02 throughout the transition regime, forcing beta effectively to zero or rendering the slip mechanism inoperative.

KC5: Early-universe constraints (BBN, primary CMB) require significant departures from GR at z ≳ 10 (i.e., S ≠ 0 or effective alpha's non-vanishing), contradicting the mandated GR recovery of the sigmoid construction.

KC6: Evidence that Alens and large-scale lensing amplitudes are ≤ LCDM at the few‑percent level across relevant redshifts, closing the lensing ‘barrier’ and leaving no parameter space with Sigma > 1 compatible with mu < 1.
status: Proposed EFT completion — not canonical baseline EFC-D
abstract: Two complementary EFT ansatze for EFC: scalar-tensor (Horndeski/EFT-DE) and vector-tensor (dynamical 4-vector J^mu). Both use sigmoid entropy field S(a) to govern GR-to-modified-gravity transition. Target: mu < 1, eta > 1, Sigma > 1.

entropy_field.equation: S(a) = [1 + exp(-(ln a - ln a_t) / Delta)]^{-1}

boundary_conditions.peak: dS/d(ln a) peaks at a = a_t

ansatz_I_scalar_tensor.name: Scalar-Tensor EFT (Horndeski)
ansatz_I_scalar_tensor.action: L = M_Pl^2/2 R + K(S,X) + G3(S,X) box S
ansatz_I_scalar_tensor.observables: mu, eta, Sigma determined by {alpha_K, alpha_B, alpha_M, alpha_T} via quasi-static limit
expected_behaviour: mu < 1 at mid-z (alpha_B, alpha_M -> 0 at high z)
eta > 1 from alpha_B != 0 (sign for B0 > 0, to be confirmed numerically)
Sigma > 1 region may exist in {B0, M0} space

ansatz_II_vector_tensor.name: Vector-Tensor EFT (Energy Flow)
ansatz_II_vector_tensor.action: L = M_Pl^2/2 R - 1/4 F_{mu nu} F^{mu nu} - m^2/2 J_mu J^mu + beta J^mu nabla_mu S
ansatz_II_vector_tensor.F_definition: F_{mu nu} = nabla_mu J_nu - nabla_nu J_mu

anisotropic_stress.energy_momentum: T_{mu nu}^(nabla S) = beta^2 [nabla_mu S nabla_nu S - 1/4 g_{mu nu} (nabla S)^2]
anisotropic_stress.shear: pi ~ beta^2 nabla S_bar . nabla delta_S
anisotropic_stress.C_eta: positive, to be determined by full perturbation analysis

falsification_criterion: No parameter region {B0, M0, a_t, Delta} with mu < 1, eta > 1, Sigma > 1 simultaneously under stability + CMB + LSS constraints in hi_class scan
open_questions: Does {B0, M0} region exist with mu < 1, eta > 1, Sigma > 1 simultaneously?
Are stability conditions Q_S > 0, c_S^2 > 0 satisfied across sigmoid transition?
What is the precise coefficient C_eta in the vector-tensor slip (Eq 21)?
Does J^mu action reduce to scalar EFT in isotropic quasi-static limit?
priority_steps: Implement alpha_B(a), alpha_M(a) with EFC sigmoid in hi_class
Run joint Planck 2018 + DESI Y1 + BOSS likelihood for {B0, M0, a_t, Delta}
Derive linearised perturbation equations for J^mu sector, compute eta(a,k)
